catalysts.headline: Department of War announced a $450 million redeemable preferred equity investment in Elmet (via its Industrial Base Analysis and Sustainment program / Economic Defense Unit; Elmet to draw $200M initially, DoW to receive preferred equity + warrants for up to 19.9% of common stock plus one independent board seat and one non-voting observer); separately, subsidiary Elmet Technologies received a Defense Logistics Agency IDIQ-type award with a $2 billion ceiling and a guaranteed funded commitment of $150 million, covering tungsten ores/concentrates and sodium tungstate for the National Defense Stockpile. Elmet plans ~$165M into US facilities and ~$150M into the Springer Tungsten Complex (Nevada).
catalysts.note: One secondary source (ManufacturingDive) dates the DLA award to 2026-09-11 rather than 2026-09-14, and frames the DoW investment as a Class A preferred stock purchase rather than the preferred-equity-plus-warrants structure described in the official war.gov release; Quartr's summary calls the DLA deal a 'framework agreement' rather than a straight award -- see conflicts.

conflicts: Theme mismatch on file: watchlist carried ELMT under 'Consumer Hardware', which is a clear mismatch -- Elmet is a tungsten/molybdenum critical-materials manufacturer (Critical Materials Components division) and now a major defense-industrial-base counterparty (DoW equity investment + DLA stockpile contract), not a consumer hardware company. Reassigned to 'Advanced Materials' here (closer fit than 'Government IT & Defense Services', which describes services/IT contractors rather than a materials producer, even though its largest current customer relationship is defense).

DoW/DLA deal structure and dates: war.gov/pulse2 describe a $450M redeemable preferred equity investment plus warrants, closing with DLA IDIQ contract reported ~2026-09-14; ManufacturingDive instead describes Class A preferred stock and dates the DLA award 2026-09-11; Quartr calls the DLA piece a 'framework agreement' rather than a definitive award.
Market cap: $411.56M at IPO (April 2026) vs $600.97M (Sept 2026 snapshot) vs $633.403M ('intraday', undated) -- no current (Oct 2026) figure confirmed.

Cash as of Q2 2026: MarketBeat/company earnings call cites $66.1M vs Simply Wall St cites cash+short-term investments of $71.0M (possibly a different line-item definition, not necessarily contradictory).
